title: E-value, bit score and database size
caption: The E-value is the number of hits of at least that score expected by chance: E = m × n × 2^−S for a query of length m, a database of n letters and a bit score S. On a log scale it falls in a straight line as the bit score rises, and a database ten times larger raises every E-value tenfold, so the same alignment is less significant.
alt: Two parallel lines of log of the E-value against bit score, falling by 0.301 per bit, the line for a ten times larger database one unit higher, with a threshold at E = 10 to the minus 5.
description: E = m × n × 2^−S, so log₁₀ E falls by 0.301 for each extra bit of score.
Here the query has 300 residues and the databases have 10⁸ and 10⁹ residues.
A 10 times larger database raises log₁₀ E by exactly 1: more chance matches are expected.
E-values below about 10⁻⁵ usually indicate meaningful similarity: that needs a bit score of about 51 (smaller database) or 55 (larger).
